tc.research_text.ARCANEASSEMBLER: The arcane version of the ME Molecular Assembler, capable of automated arcane crafting.
tc.research_text.ARCANEASSEMBLER.stage.1:
While examining the §lMolecular Assembler§r it occurs to you that it may be possible to modify the assembler to produce arcane items. You conclude that by infusing the assembler with the appropriate shards it will be able to regulate vis flow into items. It will also need a moderate amount of vis storage, and the §lSilverwood Scepter§r seems the best choice.
Note: The scepter is infused into the assembler, and must be fully charged.
tc.research_text.ARCANEASSEMBLER.stage.2:
§lPattern Storage§r
The assembler itself does not store crafting recipes. Further research may be required to devise a pattern storage medium.
§lVis Replenishment§r
Replenishing the assembler's internal vis storage will require the services of a §lVis Relay Interface§r.
§lAcceleration Cards§r
Each card decreases crafting time by 20% and increases power required by 50%.§lVis Discounts§r
Due to the inclusion of the crafting scepter, the assembler has a base vis discount equal to that of the scepter. The discount can be further enhanced by providing the assembler vis discount armor. The discount for each aspect can be viewed by hovering over the aspect in the GUI.
The assembler is not immune to the effects of warping gear; For each point of warp the assembler must draw an additional 15% power to remain stable while crafting.
tc.research_text.ARCANECRAFTINGTERMINAL: Combine an ME Terminal with an Arcane Worktable for direct arcane crafting in the ME network.
You have discovered that using primal aspects to bind a §lTerminal§r to an §lArcane Worktable§r allows you to imbue the terminal with the worktable's ability to craft arcane items.
The terminal retains its ability to access items on the ME network allowing faster and more plentiful crafting, as well as store and swap a set of armor for when you need a quick vis discount.

Put the wand in the terminal's wand slot and the grid is supplied from the network, which also covers the vis the craft comes up short of. The vis and crystals it will cost are worked out for you before you craft.
tc.research_text.BASEENERGISTICS:
As both a scientist and an arcane scholar, you have postulated that it must be possible to combine technology and magic in a stable and productive way.
You will need to study the principals of matter-energy conversion in detail to accomplish this. It is likely there are aspects of Thaumaturgy that can accomplish this, as well as technology capable of doing the same.
This will require extensive study, but you are sure that it will be a worthwhile investment of your time.
High-version textures drawn by @麦淇淋.
tc.research_text.CERTUS_DUPE: Using alchemical duplication, you can duplicate certus quartz crystals. This provides a renewable source of certus quartz for your AE network.
tc.research_text.DIGISENTIA: Digitize essentia using Diffusion and Coalescence Cores for processing by the ME network.
tc.research_text.DIGISENTIA.stage.1:
Having discovered how to distill essentia, it occurs to you that you may be able store it digitally.
Examining the §lFormation Core§r and §lAnnihilation Core§r you realize that with some minor modifications they could serve as a means to convert essentia to and from a digital format.
However, due to the corrosive nature of certain types of essentia, a layer of quicksilver around the circuitry is required to prevent decay.
tc.research_text.DIGISENTIA.stage.2:
§lDiffusion Core§r
The relatively high volatility and immense energy in distilled essentia requires that it first be diffused then digitized. A buffer chamber of some kind will likely be required to hold the diffused essentia.§lCoalescence Core§r
Compresses and binds re-materialized essentia diffusion back into its raw form. A buffer chamber will also likely be needed.
tc.research_text.DISTILLATIONENCODER:
Expanding on the principals of AE's autocrafing system, you have created a way to encode the essentia distillation process onto an §lEncoded Pattern§r.
Placing an item into the Thaumometer slot will reveal what you know of the items composition. After selecting the preferred aspect, it can then be encoded onto the encoded pattern or an available blank pattern.
tc.research_text.ESSENTIACELLWORKBENCH.s: A cell that accepts anything will fill up with the first aspect that reaches it. I need a way to tell a cell which aspects it is allowed to hold before it ever enters the network.

The essentia cell workbench writes a partition onto a cell: place the cell in the top slot and drag aspects into the wells, and the network will refuse to store anything else in it. Clicking "partition to contents" fills the wells from what the cell already holds.
tc.research_text.ESSENTIALEVELEMITTER: The §lEssentia Level Emitter§r provides a redstone signal when the level of essentia in the network falls below or rises above a set amount.
tc.research_text.ALCHEMYPROVIDER: Automatically extracts essentia from the ME network and supplies adjacent containers.
tc.research_text.ALCHEMYPROVIDER.connect:
Import and export buses only reach what stands right beside them. To carry a provider further afield, you built the §lAlchemy Wireless Receiver§r.
The receiver mounts on any surface and links to a provider with the §lWireless Binding Tool§r. Essentia then crosses between the two, sixteen at a time, and whatever a neighbouring container holds can be sent back into the network. The receiver stores nothing itself.
One provider serves at most eight receivers, no more than thirty-two blocks apart; each receiver it carries adds five to its idle draw.
tc.research_text.ALCHEMYPROVIDER.stage.1:
While import and export buses are useful for an array of jobs, they lack the flexibility to interface with complex alchemical constructs. To overcome this limitation you have created a device that will allow these constructs to request any essentia directly from the network.
Using the §lEssentia Provider§r should prove to be a simple task. Simply connect it to both the network and construct, and it will do the rest.
Like an essentia buffer it has a small amount of suction(8).
tc.research_text.ALCHEMYPROVIDER.stage.2: Set the Alchemy Provider against the container you want filled and it works on its own: it draws from the network and pushes whatever the neighbour will take, for as long as the network holds that aspect. Nothing has to be configured.
tc.research_text.ALCHEMYPROVIDER.tool.st:
The §lWireless Binding Tool§r joins a receiver to a provider: sneak-right-click a receiver to select it, then sneak-right-click a provider to complete the link. A plain right-click on either end reports where it is and what it is bound to.
Beyond the distance or count limit the link is refused, and the tool says which limit was hit.
tc.research_text.ESSENTIASTORAGE: Using Coalescence Cores and wisp essences, you can create ME storage cells capable of storing essentia. Available in 1k, 4k, 16k, and 64k variants.
tc.research_text.ESSENTIASTORAGE16k.stag: The same trick again, now with engineering-grade circuitry in the binding. Sixteen times the capacity of a single component.
The 16k component is complete. Essentia density this high needs careful casing, but it holds.
tc.research_text.ESSENTIASTORAGE1k.stage:
Upon inspecting existing digital storage mediums you have concluded that you can in-fact store digitized essentia.
By infusing §lCertus Quartz§r with concentrated essence, it will gain the ability to store the essentia, which remains remarkably active even in digital form.
You conclude that the higher the concentration of essence, the more it should be able to store, although there are inherit limits as to how much the quartz itself can store.
The 1k essentia storage component and its cell are complete. Eight thousand esssential units fit in a single cell, far more than any jar could hold, and the network reads it as ordinary storage.
tc.research_text.ESSENTIASTORAGE4k.stage: One component is not enough. By binding three 1k components into a single casing I should be able to hold four times as much.
The 4k component is stable and its cell holds four times the essentia of the 1k.
tc.research_text.ESSENTIASTORAGE64k.stag: The final tier. The calculations are considerably more demanding than the previous ones, and the casing must be flawless.
The 64k component is finished. It holds sixty-four times the capacity of a single component, enough essentia to run a serious alchemical operation from the network alone.
tc.research_text.ESSENTIATERMINAL: View and manage all essentia stored in your ME network.
The §lEssentia Terminal§r provides a convenient way to insert or extract essentia stored within the network.
When placing a jar or phial it will be emptied if it contains any essentia, or filled with the selected aspect. Labels can also be set or cleared depending on the selected aspect.

For the Thaumaturge with little time on their hands and many aspects to work with, the displayed aspects can be clicked with an item to fill, drain, or set the item in question.
When holding multiple of an item, items will be returned to your inventory.
tc.research_text.ESSENTIAVIBRATIONCHAMBE:
Every AE my network has had came from burning things in the §lVibration Chamber§r. Essentia already holds the energy; why burn coal to reach it?
So I built the §lEssentia Vibration Chamber§r. Essentia burns inside it a point at a time; the power it gives off lands in a buffer of its own, and the network draws on that. It generates nothing new. All it does is take what the network would have burned anyway and burn a better fuel.§l§nOperation§r
Feed it whatever you mean to burn; whatever went in last is what it pays by.
The suction gave me trouble: it pulls essentia to itself, so the moment its buffer fills it stops burning and withdraws the suction.
Three bars show the buffer, the fuel, and the power waiting inside.§l§nNotes§r
It fits in an §lEssentia Terminal§r, and tubes or the §lEssentia Export Bus§r keep it fed.
It idles when the network has power to spare, but turns down no aspect.
tc.research_text.FOCUS_AEWRENCH:
This wand focus interacts with blocks and machinery as if it were an AE2 wrench.
Sneak + left click: Rotate.
Sneak + right click: Dismantle.
tc.research_text.GOLEMWIFI:
After watching your golems running around depositing gathered items into a chest for you to collect and store later, you wondered if you could cut out the middle-man. Inspiration struck when you realized that you could utilize your networks wireless capabilities to do just that.
After spending hours feverishly working, you created a backpack that will give your golems access to the network. The backpack does come with some limitations however. Golems must be in range of an §lAccess Point§r to communicate with the network. The fluix pearl atop the antenna serves as an indicator to whether or not the golem can communicate with the network.As communicating with the network takes power, you retro-fitted a charger to draw power from two embedded Nitor. When charged the backpack will be able to transmit for only a short time before starting another charge cycle. During this window of opportunity the golem will be able to interact with the network.
To link the backpack with your network, place it in the security terminal.As you progress with your golemancy research, check back here for potential new uses of the backpack.§nFacades§r
Facades can be used to apply a variety of styles to the backpack: Thaumium Block(default), Greatwood Log, Bricks, Hay Bale, Tallow Block, Flesh Block, Stone, Iron Block, Gold Block and Diamond Block.
Right click on a golem wearing a backpack with the facade in hand to apply it.
tc.research_text.OCCULTMONITOR.stage.1:
The §lOccult Monitor§r watches an Infusion Altar. It shows the main facts of the ritual above itself: what is being infused, how stable the altar stands, how dangerous the ritual is, and how much of every aspect is still missing or left over.
Before it counts anything missing it checks what the altar can reach, jars, providers and the network's own stock among them.
The instant an infusion completes, the monitor also emits a redstone pulse.
tc.research_text.OCCULTMONITOR.stage.2:
It has to hang within twelve blocks of the altar, be wired into the ME network, and hold a §lThaumonomicon§r in its slot. Without the tome it is a lump of metal.
The bubble is drawn over the monitor's own head and is visible within eight blocks, though its words read through walls. The same readings are written into the block's tooltip, with a line on what this risk tier means.
To take the tome back, sneak with an empty hand and right-click the monitor.
tc.research_text.INFUSIONPROVIDER: Automatically supplies essentia from the ME network to an Infusion Altar.
While studying infusion it occurs to you that the altar only ever asks for a container of essentia nearby, and never minds where that essentia came from. So the network can be that container: when the altar reaches for a point, the essentia is taken out of its digital form and handed over.
The §lInfusion Provider§r is such a device. It stores no essentia of its own, and fetches a point from the network only when the altar reaches for it.
Because it holds nothing, a pipe will not pump it like a jar, and the altar cannot push essentia back into it.

It belongs anywhere the altar can reach: twelve blocks in every direction, of which underneath is merely the handiest spot. Once it is on the ME network, whatever aspect the altar reaches for is fetched from the network on the spot, a point at a time, and leaves as a stream of light towards the altar.
It idles at five AE a tick. With the network unpowered, or with the block unwired, it is no more use than plain stone.
With it, jars are no longer required. When another machine takes that essentia out of the network, however, the altar goes short again.
tc.research_text.KNOWLEDGECORE:
With the §lArcane Assembler§r constructed, you will need a way to teach it what it will be assembling.
You have devised the §lKnowledge Core§r, a device capable of storing arcane recipes. The core serves as pattern storage, giving the assembler instructions on how to build items.
To encode recipe patterns on the core, you will need to use the §lKnowledge Inscriber§r.
tc.research_text.KNOWLEDGEINSCRIBER: The Knowledge Inscriber converts Thaumaturgical research notes into Knowledge Cores that the AE network can recognize. It bridges the gap between arcane knowledge and digital storage.
tc.research_text.KNOWLEDGEINSCRIBER.stag:
With the §lArcane Assembler§r constructed, you will need a way to teach it what it will be assembling.
You have devised the §lKnowledge Core§r, a device capable of storing arcane recipes. The core serves as pattern storage, giving the assembler instructions on how to build items.
To encode recipe patterns on the core, you will need to use the §lKnowledge Inscriber§r.

Using The §lKnowledge Inscriber§r
First place a §lKnowledge Core§r into the top-right slot. Next, use the crafting grid to setup the recipe for the item. If you have the required knowledge(research) for the recipe, the resulting item will be displayed. Pressing the save button will then inscribe the recipe onto the core. The finished product will then show in the stored-pattern area.
To remove an inscribed recipe from the core, first select a pattern from the stored-pattern area. The selected patterns recipe will then display in the crafting area. Finally, clicking the delete button will remove the pattern from the core.
tc.research_text.VISINTERFACE:
Having discovered the vis power network, you now pursue the means of linking your digital system to this network.
After observing how vis flows through the network of §lvis relays§r, you believe you can construct a digital device to harness the vis. By utilizing the peer-to-peer capabilities of the digital network, vis can be imported, tunnelled, and used by your digital devices.
Storing it however, will require more research.To use the §lVis Relay Interface§r, attach it to the digital network and place a vis relay on it. The base of the relay must be against the interface.
In order for a device to receive vis it must be linked with the interface. Linking other devices to the interface will require the use of a §lMemory Card§r. Each device can only be linked with one interface.
Shift right-click on the interface with a memory card, then right-click on a device to create the link.
Right clicking the other device with a blank memory card will remove the link.§lLinks§r§lVis Relay Interface§r.Constructs a P2P vis tunnel.
§lArcane Crafting Terminal§r. Charges the wand in the A.C.T.
§lArcane Assembler§r. Fills vis storage, used for crafting.
tc.research_text.WIRELESSESSENTIATERMINA: Carrying a terminal to the jar is a waste of walking. The same wireless receiver an ME network already uses for its wireless terminal should carry essentia just as well.

The wireless essentia terminal links to a network through a wireless access point and shows its essentia from anywhere in range. Bind it to a network by using it, exactly as an ME wireless terminal is bound.

tc.research_text.ESSENTIAACCESSCARD.stag: An ME interface reads items and fluids. A §lBasic Card§r infused with a diffusion core gives it the rest of the job: the aspects you mark on the interface's own config row are pulled out of the machine beside it and into the network.

Fit the card to an ME interface, one for the block form and one for the cable part, then mark the aspects you want on its config row, and it lets those aspects into the ME network. The same card also goes into an arcane crafting terminal's upgrade slot, where it gives the terminal its essentia gestures.
tc.research_text.FLUXTRANSFERINTERFACE.s:
A §lVis Relay Interface§r carries vis from the network to wherever it is wanted. The reverse also works: vis can be drawn out of the network and burned into flux. The §lFlux Transfer Interface§r is the device that does it, used in pairs - one end draws vis and ordo out of the network, the other decides which chunk the flux falls in.
By your reckoning one cycle leaves about as much flux behind as a crucible's leftovers. Flux seeps into the local aura the moment it is made, and it can be neither jarred nor carried, so the vent can only be where the interface itself stands.

A pair of §lFlux Transfer Interfaces§r is bound together with a §lMemory Card§r: one end takes the vis and ordo out of the network, the other pours flux into the chunk it stands in.
Placement is the one thing to watch. The flux falls where the interface is, so the vent belongs away from crystals, golems and crops.
If the network has nowhere to put tainted essentia, an §lME Drive§r for instance, the surplus falls in the controller's chunk, and a controller is no better a neighbour for a field than a vent is.
It is not wholly reliable: one cycle in ten condenses the flux into tainted essentia and puts it straight into the network's storage, and about 1.5% of cycles do not condense it at all but seep it out around the controller. With no controller on the grid, both cases land beside a drive or the interface itself.
tc.research_text.GACHABOX.stage.1:
You can hold essentia in frozen light, and you can read the aura around an altar. Put the two together and the problem is simple: essentia is potential, and potential can be traded for something else.
The knowledge it brings is not conjured out of nothing - it is borrowed against the aura around it, and the aura collects. A §lBrain in a Jar§r, properly bound, carries that cost for a while; the box only completes the exchange.
tc.research_text.GACHABOX.stage.2:
§lA Gacha Box§r is infused as a body, with a §lKnowledge Core§r in place of a mundane frame, and it knows how to trade essentia for knowledge.
It must be bound to a §lBrain in a Jar§r before it will run, a binding made by right-clicking the box with the jar in hand. It remembers who bound it, and only that player can take the brain back out. Beyond the binding it wants a channel, power, and cognitio in the pipe.
§lThe Gacha Box Aggregator§r is the lid it wears, and without it the frame is unfinished.Its figures are these: a turn runs from 30 seconds to 3 minutes, and a full set of speed cards shortens the longest to 80 seconds. The faster it turns the likelier it pays - 75% of the shortest turns pay, 45% of the longest. When it pays it hands over 5 to 7 draws, 1 to 3 points each, theory and observation at even odds.Its return is not fixed, and the moment it pays is not yours to choose.
tc.research_text.VISCONNECTIONCARD.stage: Most upgrade cards in AE2 are a §lBasic Card§r with a part added. Infuse one with a crystal that resonates with the aura and the machine it sits in stops buying vis from the network, taking it from the aura around it instead.

Infuse a basic card with an §lAuram Vis Crystal§r and fit it into an arcane crafting terminal's upgrade slot. The craft then takes its untyped vis straight from the aura around the terminal, or around the player when the terminal is the one being carried; the network pays none of it.
tc.research_text.WIRELESSARCANECRAFTINGT: The arcane crafting terminal is bound to the worktable it was built on and can only be used nearby. The receiver that carries a network as far as an essentia terminal should carry this worktable to the player just as well.

Bind the wireless arcane crafting terminal to an access point as you would any ME wireless terminal, and it opens the same grid as the placed one, wand slot included. An essentia access card in one upgrade slot lets the terminal use the network's essentia; a vis connection card in the other takes the craft's vis from the aura around the player.
